v.title: Beattie & Haughey: A Fresh Spark for NI's Strikers
v.excerpt: Beattie returns, Haughey debuts – McArdle’s bold move could reshape NI’s attack for the Euro race.
v.body:
## Quick take
Kerry Beattie returns and Ella Haughey gets her first cap – a bold move by Michael McArdle that could reshape Northern Ireland’s attack ahead of the Euro qualifiers.

## What happened
McArdle, who has been juggling a tight schedule, announced that striker Kerry Beattie will rejoin the squad after a brief spell out of favour. Beattie, who scored six times in his last 12 internationals, is expected to add a physical presence up front. Alongside him, the 20‑year‑old Ella Haughey, who has yet to earn a cap, is called up for the friendly double‑header against Greece. Haughey, a versatile winger with a knack for cutting inside, will be the first uncapped player since 2018.

The pair will feature in two back‑to‑back friendlies, giving the manager a chance to test a more attacking line‑up. McArdle’s decision signals a shift from the more conservative approach of the past, aiming to inject pace and goal‑scoring prowess into a team that has struggled to convert chances.

## Why it matters
- **Beattie’s return could tighten NI’s front line**: With his aerial threat and work rate, Beattie can complement the existing forwards, providing a target for long balls and a link‑up player for the creative midfield. Barcelona fans know how a physical striker can change the dynamic of a game.
- **Haughey’s debut brings fresh creativity**: Her ability to drift inside from the wing and deliver precise through balls could add a new dimension to NI’s attack. For a club like Barcelona, where technical flair is prized, Haughey’s profile mirrors that of the club’s youth prospects.
- **Long‑term squad building**: Introducing a young player like Haughey alongside an experienced forward signals a long‑term plan. It mirrors Barcelona’s philosophy of blending youth with seasoned talent, potentially setting a blueprint for future national teams.

## What's next
Watch the first match against Greece for Beattie’s impact on the build‑up play and Haughey’s integration into the attacking third. Key moments to spot: Beattie’s aerial duels, Haughey’s first touch and any early goal contributions. Their performances will determine whether McArdle’s gamble pays off and whether Northern Ireland can adopt a more dynamic, Barcelona‑style attacking philosophy.

*Source: [Can returning Beattie and Haughey make an impact?](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cm04wz6ez2rgo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
